simple.meaning: כָּנַס (kânaç) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to collect ; hence, to enfold.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 11 times across 1 Chronicles, Nehemiah, Esther, Psalms, Ecclesiastes, and 2 more, beginning at 1 Chronicles 22:2. Its contexts include family line, offering, Torah, kingship, priesthood, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּנַס (H3664).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כָּנַס (kânaç) / H3664 is traced through 1 Chronicles 22:2, Nehemiah 12:44, Esther 4:16, Psalms 33:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: David gave orders to gather together the foreigners who were in the land of Israel; and he set masons to cut dressed stones to build God’s house.

On that day, men were appointed over the rooms for the treasures, for the wave offerings, for the first fruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them, according to the fields of the cities, the portions appointed by the law for the priests and Levites; for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites who waited.

“Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Susa, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.”
He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap.

I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men: musical instruments, and that of all sorts.

For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
a time to cast away stones,
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.
Yes, I will gather you, and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you will be melted in the middle of it.
They will know that I am Yahweh their God, in that I caused them to go into captivity among the nations, and have gathered them to their own land. Then I will leave none of them captive any more.

definitions.full: H3664. kanas [ כָּנַס ] verb gather, collect (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic כְּנַס (see also כנשׁ ); Ethiopic in derived conjugation assemble for worship , etc.; Arabic is sweep, sweep away, destroy ) — Qal (late) Perfect 1singular כָּנַסְתִּי Eccl 2:8 ; Imperative כְּנוֺס Est 4:16 ; Infinitive construct 1Chr 22:2-3 t.; Participle כֹּנֵס Psa 33:7 ; — gather people 1Chr 22:2 ; Est 4:16 ; ׳כ תְּהוֺמוֺת בְּאוֺצָרוֺת נֹתֵן הַיָּ֑ם מֵי כַּנֵּד Psa 33:7 (read perhaps, for כַּנּאֹד כַּנֵּד, as in a wine skin , see נד נאד, ); gather, collect portions of harvest for priests and Levites Neh 12:44 ; stones Eccl 3:5 (opposed to השׁליך ); silver and gold = amass wealth 2:8 ; absolute 2:26 (|| אסף ). Pi`el Perfect 1singular אֶתְכֶם וְכִנַּסְתִּ֫י Ezek 22:21 and I will gather you together (for punishment; Co translates to 22:20 and reads for וְהִנַּחְתִּ֫י ; || קבץ 22:19 ; 22:20 ); of restoration אֶלאַֿדְמָתָם וְכִנַּסְתִּים 39:28 , and יְכַנֵּס Psa 147:2 . Hithpa`el Infinitive construct צָרָה כְּהִתְכַּנֵּסוְהַמַּסֵּכָה Isa 28:20 and the covering is (too) narrow when one gathers oneself together (|| הַמַּצָּע מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַקָצַר ), i.e. the bed is too short to stretch oneself at full length, and when one (perforce) draws up the feet, the covering becomes too narrow.
